items.title: Fontaines D.C. Preview New Album ‘Dopamine Chamber’ With Song ‘Marianne’
items.summary:
Fontaines D.C. have announced their fifth album. Dopamine Chamber arrives Oct. 16 on XL Recordings, and the Irish band released the lead single, "Marianne," alongside the announcement.

"Marianne" sits in the same post-punk register as 2024's Romance, built on atmospheric drums and dark guitar, with frontman Grian Chatten coaxing the listener in: "This year, you should come and stay here," he sings. "You can follow my lead/I can help you disappear." Rolling Stone reported that the song draws partial inspiration from the 2024 miniseries Ripley, which starred Andrew Scott.

James Ford, who produced Romance, returned for the new record. A press release frames the album's subject matter as the contents of the endless scroll — artificial intelligence, celebrity gossip, political violence, climate collapse and the memes they generate. "The album itself is a dopamine chamber," Chatten said in a statement. "You step inside and we test these different mind or mood-altering pieces of music on you."

Bassist Conor Deegan described the band's records as a running interrogation of place. "First Dublin, then being away from Dublin, and then trying to find the romance elsewhere," he said. "On this record, the question became: where do you escape to?" Chatten wrote parts of the album while traveling through Venice, Sicily and Vienna, and the band recorded in London, the English countryside and Palermo, where Chatten assembled a vocal booth out of mattresses and cushions.

Chatten put a number on the shift between the two albums. "I think Romance was maybe 60 percent human and 40 percent corrupted by automation, and a loss of feeling," he said. "This one feels more like 60 percent corrupted — the mask is wearing the face a little more. I felt it would be more powerful to leave the hope out and reflect the ugliness honestly. This one needed to feel more like a catastrophic warning."

Romance earned a Mercury Prize nomination and two nods at the 67th Grammy Awards, for Best Rock Album and, for "Starburster," Best Alternative Music Performance. The band has European and American festival dates booked through late September, including Reading and Leeds, Shaky Knees, Electric Picnic and Sea.Hear.Now.

items.title: Madonna Leads 2026 MTV VMA Nominations: Full List
items.summary:
Madonna leads the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards with 11 nominations, the most of any artist and a career best for her. It is the first time she has topped the nominations list since 1998, when "Ray of Light" won her a first video of the year trophy. She also led in 1990 with "Vogue," taking nine nods in both of those years.

Her 14-minute "Confessions II – The Film" is up for video of the year, following two recent long-form winners in the category: Taylor Swift's "All Too Well: The Short Film" in 2022 and Ariana Grande's 26-minute "Brighter Days Ahead" last year. Swift, who holds the record with 30 Moon Persons, is second this year with nine nominations. Grande and Sabrina Carpenter have seven each, Bruno Mars, PinkPantheress and Zara Larsson five each, and LISA four — seven of the eight most-nominated artists are women.

The video of the year field also includes Grande's "hate that i made you love me," Swift's "The Fate of Ophelia," Mars' "I Just Might," Carpenter's "Tears" and GENER8ION's "Storm," an audiovisual project from French DJ Surkin and director Romain Gavras starring Swedish rapper Yung Lean as a disruptive boarding school student. In artist of the year, Grande picks up a record-extending sixth nomination and Swift her fifth, with Mars, Carpenter, Morgan Wallen and, for the first time, Madonna rounding out the category. Billboard noted that no hip-hop artists were nominated there for the first time since the category began in 2017, and no Latin artists for the first time in five years.

Best new artist nominees are Bella Kay, CORTIS, Magnus Ferrell, Malcolm Todd, Myles Smith, Sienna Spiro and Stella Lefty. Best dance returns after a seven-year absence, with Madonna competing against Bebe Rexha and Faithless, Harry Styles, Lady Gaga and Doechii, PinkPantheress and Larsson, Slayyyter and Tate McRae. Several categories from last year's show, including best rock, best Afrobeats, best pop artist, best album, best group and song of summer, did not appear in the initial announcement.

Fan voting opened in 13 categories at vote.MTV.com and runs through Sept. 25 at 6 p.m. ET, with best new artist staying open into the broadcast. Double votes are available during a daily "Power Hour" from 1 to 2 p.m. ET between Aug. 20 and Sept. 24.

CBS will air the ceremony live from the Peacock Theatre in Los Angeles on Sunday, Sept. 27 from 7:30 to 9:30 p.m. ET, simulcast on MTV and streaming on Paramount+. It is the show's first time in the Los Angeles area since Katy Perry hosted from The Forum in 2017, its second consecutive year on CBS, and the first VMAs held in the fall rather than late summer. Gunpowder & Sky produces, with Van Toffler returning as producer.

items.title: Ellie Goulding Sues Ex-Management Company Over Live Nation Ties
items.summary:
Ellie Goulding has sued her former management company in the U.K., alleging that the firm's ownership by Live Nation created conflicts of interest that it never disclosed to her. Rolling Stone obtained the suit, which names TaP Management co-founders Benedict Mawson and Edward Millett along with HNOE, the Live Nation entity that took control of the company.

Goulding was a TaP client from 2018 to 2025. Her filing notes that Live Nation acquired a 50.1 percent stake in the firm through HNOE in 2015 and bought the remainder in 2019. She alleges her management team never told her about that ownership and repeatedly steered her toward Live Nation and its subsidiaries for concert promotion, merchandise and a documentary.

The suit argues the defendants had financial and commercial reasons to keep her business inside the Live Nation group, breaching their duty to secure her the best available terms. "Each of the Defendants had a personal interest or duty in dealings between Ms. Goulding and companies in the Live Nation group, which was in actual or potential conflict with the interests of Ms Goulding in securing the best commercial terms with whichever promoter, merchandiser, or other counterparty it was most advantageous for her to deal with," it states. Goulding is seeking unspecified compensation and damages plus additional relief.

Live Nation is not a defendant. Mawson, Millett and TaP did not immediately respond to requests for comment, and a representative for Goulding declined to comment.

Goulding joined TaP in 2018, when its roster included Lana Del Rey and Dua Lipa, following her 2015 album Delirium, which reached No. 3 in both the U.K. and the U.S. and produced the single "On My Mind." She stayed with the firm through 2020's Brightest Blue and 2023's Higher Than Heaven. The two sides split in December 2025, with The Sun reporting conflicting accounts — a source on Goulding's side said she left the arrangement, while a source close to TaP said the firm resigned on Dec. 9 after eight years.

Goulding's sixth studio album, I Know Too Much, is scheduled for release Sept. 4.

items.title: ABC Sues FCC Over Threats to Broadcast Licenses In First Amendment Case
items.summary:
ABC sued the Federal Communications Commission on Tuesday in D.C. District Court, arguing that the agency's scrutiny of its broadcast licenses and of The View amounts to a First Amendment violation by the Trump administration. The Disney-owned network asked the court to halt early license renewal proceedings for its eight stations and sought a temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction.

The network filed now because the comment period on the renewal applications has closed, leaving the FCC free to issue an order at any point that would trigger formal hearings on all eight licenses. "If the Administration gets its way, the message to every media company in the country will be unmistakable: tell only the stories the Administration deems favorable, or face the coercive machinery of the federal government," the complaint reads. "In such a world, the press could in no way be described as free."

The FCC called the licenses in for early renewal earlier this year, a step ABC took under protest. The suit notes the commission had not demanded an early renewal application in more than half a century and had never sought simultaneous early filings from a group of stations commonly owned with a single network. ABC points out that the order came a day after the administration called for action against Jimmy Kimmel over a joke about Trump, and quotes the FCC chairman telling an interviewer, "If you didn't take us seriously, now you should."

The Hollywood Reporter noted the suit also cites Trump's Truth Social posts calling for revocation of ABC's and NBC's licenses after neither carried his July 16 primetime address live. ABC weighed the risk of retaliation and ultimately livestreamed the speech on ABC News LIVE, something the complaint says it would not ordinarily have done.

A separate FCC proceeding concerns The View, which the agency contends is not a bona fide news program and therefore not exempt from equal opportunity rules — a position that followed a February appearance by James Talarico, the Democratic Senate nominee in Texas. ABC says no candidate has appeared on the show since, and that producers have withheld certain video clips out of concern about the license renewals. The network says it has answered more than 600 requests and produced more than 13,000 pages of documents across both investigations.

ABC argues that any FCC adjudication would be "a charade," with the agency either dragging out the process at mounting cost or moving to revoke the licenses outright. "In either scenario, the Administration accomplishes its goal of eliminating a perceived media critic: either it gets Plaintiffs to fall in line, or it silences them if they refuse," the suit reads. The FCC did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

items.title: Jackson Lamb’s Team Hunted Like Prey In ‘Slow Horses’ Season 6 Trailer; Olivia Cooke Returns
items.summary:
Apple TV has released the trailer for Slow Horses Season 6, which puts Jackson Lamb's crew of exiled MI5 agents on the run. The footage shows Gary Oldman's Lamb and his Slough House team caught up in a campaign of retaliation and revenge driven by Kristin Scott Thomas' Diana Taverner.

The trailer leans on the show's comic register early. "I cannot emphasize this enough: Stay dark, yeah? No phones," Lamb barks — immediately followed by a cut to hacker Roddy Ho, played by Christopher Chang, ringing him on a cell. "What don't you understand about going dark?" Lamb shouts back.

The bigger reveal is the return of Olivia Cooke as Sid Baker, the agent last seen at the end of Season 1. Deadline reported that she appears at the top of a staircase waiting for Jack Lowden's River Cartwright, greeting him with a smirk and a "Hello River" as he stops in his tracks.

The six-episode season adapts Mick Herron's Joe Country and Slough House novels, with a cast that includes Saskia Reeves, Aimee-Ffion Edwards, Rosalind Eleazar, Joanna Scanlan, Samuel West, Ruth Bradley, Tom Brooke, Jonathan Pryce, Hugo Weaving and newcomer Lenny Rush. Gaby Chiappe adapted the season as co-executive producer, and Adam Randall returns to direct.

See-Saw Films produces for Apple TV, with Jamie Laurenson, Hakan Kousetta, Julian Stevens, Iain Canning, Emile Sherman, Randall, Gail Mutrux, Douglas Urbanski and Oldman among the executive producers. Season 6 premieres Sept. 16, just under a year after Season 5, which drew nine Primetime Emmy nominations.
